title: The n-Point Telescoping Reverse Triangle Inequality
description: The parent triangle-inequality-oq-06 records the three-point reverse triangle inequality |d(x,z) − d(y,z)| ≤ d(x,y) and explicitly poses, as an open question, its n-point telescoping refinement. This child answers it: for any polygonal chain x₀, x₁, …, xₙ and any fixed reference point w, |d(x₀,w) − d(xₙ,w)| ≤ Σ d(xᵢ,xᵢ₊₁) — the distance from a moving point to a fixed reference changes by at most the total length of the path it travels. The n = 1 case recovers the parent reverse inequality. The new content is the SHARPNESS layer: for any monotone real chain a₀ ≤ ⋯ ≤ aₙ ≤ w the bound is an EQUALITY, so no coefficient can be lowered and no edge dropped.

meta.author: Classical (metric geometry); formalized in Lean 4 with Mathlib
meta.packagingNote: Tier C follow-up that answers an open question posed verbatim in the parent triangle-inequality-oq-06 gallery entry. The core inequality is a two-step composition of the Mathlib lemmas abs_dist_sub_le (three-point reverse) and dist_le_range_sum_dist (polygon/path inequality), so the inequality itself is short. The genuinely new content is the sharpness layer: telescoping_reverse_triangle_sharp_mono proves that for every monotone real chain a₀ ≤ ⋯ ≤ aₙ ≤ w the telescoping bound is an equality (both sides equal aₙ − a₀, the right via Finset.sum_range_sub telescoping), certifying the inequality cannot be improved, plus an explicit numeric witness (0,1,2 chain, w = 10). Status is verified (0 sorries, 0 axioms — only propext/Classical.choice/Quot.sound).

mathlibDependencies.description: Three-point reverse triangle inequality: |dist x z − dist y z| ≤ dist x y

overview.historicalContext: The forward triangle inequality is one of the three defining axioms of a metric space; its reverse companion |d(x,z) − d(y,z)| ≤ d(x,y) is the workhorse behind continuity of the metric and stability of distance estimates. The parent gallery entry triangle-inequality-oq-06 bundled the reverse family together with its sharpness and explicitly left open the n-point telescoping refinement: what happens when the two endpoints are joined not by a single edge but by a whole polygonal chain? This entry answers that question. The result is the reverse companion of the classical polygon (path) inequality d(x₀,xₙ) ≤ Σ d(xᵢ,xᵢ₊₁): where the polygon inequality bounds the distance between the chain's endpoints, the telescoping reverse inequality bounds how much a single point's distance to a fixed reference can change as it walks along the chain.
overview.problemStatement:
In a pseudometric space $\alpha$, for any chain $f : \mathbb{N} \to \alpha$, any $n$, and any reference point $w$:

$$\bigl|\, d(f_0, w) - d(f_n, w) \,\bigr| \;\le\; \sum_{i=0}^{n-1} d(f_i, f_{i+1}).$$

The $n = 1$ case recovers the three-point reverse inequality $|d(x,w) - d(y,w)| \le d(x,y)$. Moreover the bound is sharp: for any monotone real chain $a_0 \le a_1 \le \cdots \le a_n \le w$ it is an equality, both sides equalling $a_n - a_0$.
overview.proofStrategy: The core inequality composes two Mathlib facts: the three-point reverse inequality abs_dist_sub_le gives |d(f₀,w) − d(fₙ,w)| ≤ d(f₀,fₙ), and the polygon inequality dist_le_range_sum_dist gives d(f₀,fₙ) ≤ Σ d(fᵢ,fᵢ₊₁); chaining with .trans yields the result. The faithful stated form adds a nonnegative chain sum to the plain reverse bound. The sharpness theorem is the original work: for a monotone real chain each edge distance dist(aᵢ,aᵢ₊₁) opens to aᵢ₊₁ − aᵢ (sign fixed by monotonicity), so the path sum telescopes to aₙ − a₀ via Finset.sum_range_sub; on the left, w lies beyond the whole chain, so both reference distances open cleanly and their difference is exactly aₙ − a₀. An explicit 0,1,2 chain with w = 10 pins a concrete witness.
keyInsights: The telescoping reverse inequality is the reverse companion of the polygon inequality: the polygon inequality bounds the endpoint distance d(x₀,xₙ), while this bounds the change in a fixed reference distance along the chain — and both are controlled by the same total path length.
The n = 1 case is exactly the parent three-point reverse inequality, so the whole reverse-triangle family sits inside this single telescoping statement.

Sharpness is not incidental: any monotone real chain lying left of the reference point attains the bound with equality, because both the left difference and the right path sum collapse to aₙ − a₀. Hence no coefficient can be lowered and no edge dropped.
The proof cleanly separates the trivial composition (the inequality) from the substantive attainment result (the sharpness family), which is where the mathematical content lives.

conclusion.summary: We proved the n-point telescoping reverse triangle inequality |d(x₀,w) − d(xₙ,w)| ≤ Σ d(xᵢ,xᵢ₊₁), the open question posed in the parent triangle-inequality-oq-06 entry, showed it specialises at n = 1 to the parent three-point reverse inequality, and recorded the faithful side-point form. The new content is the sharpness family: for every monotone real chain a₀ ≤ ⋯ ≤ aₙ ≤ w the bound is an equality, both sides equalling aₙ − a₀, with an explicit numeric witness. All six theorems are fully machine-checked with 0 sorries and 0 axioms (only propext/Classical.choice/Quot.sound).
conclusion.implications: The telescoping reverse inequality is the quantitative statement that a point's distance to a fixed reference is 1-Lipschitz along any polygonal path — the same fact that underlies continuity of the metric, now with an explicit path-length bound. The monotone-chain sharpness certificate shows the bound is best-possible for an entire family, mirroring the sharpness discipline of the parent entry.
openQuestions: Characterise the full equality locus of the telescoping bound in a general geodesic space: presumably the chain must lie on a geodesic and the reference point beyond its far endpoint.
State the two-sided quadrilateral telescoping refinement, where both the start and the end of the chain are themselves joined to two distinct reference points, and determine its attainment condition.
